The Senate’s proposed tax-and-spending package is projected to add $3.3 trillion to the national deficit, while also making significant cuts to crucial federal programs like Medicaid and SNAP that many families in South Texas depend on.

These programs are lifelines in our region, providing access to health care, nutrition, and economic stability for seniors, children, and working families. Scaling them back to help fund tax cuts for the wealthiest Americans risks deepening the challenges already faced by rural communities.

We need thoughtful, fiscally responsible legislation that supports long-term growth while protecting the needs of our residents. I am committed to working with colleagues on both sides of the aisle to ensure federal policy meets the real needs of #TX28.

Today at 7:00pm CT, I’ll be hosting a telephone town hall with special guests from across the district who serve in key leadership roles within our local health care system. We’ll be discussing Medicaid – and I’ll be sharing how I’m fighting to protect both Medicaid and Medicare as they come under attack.

Join us for an update on the work I’m doing on behalf of the people of #TX28! RSVP here: https://t.co/KYEeajkfMu

My Laredo Outreach Coordinator, Melissa Peña, presented Congressional Certificates of Recognition to two outstanding teams at Laredo Medical Center, the ICU unit and the dedicated team on Floor 5C.

These healthcare professionals exemplify not only clinical excellence but also extraordinary compassion and humanity. Their care extends beyond medicine, offering comfort to patients and families during their most difficult moments and providing calm in times of crisis.

We thank them for their unwavering dedication and the profound impact they make in our community every day.

On July 30, 1965, President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Medicare and Medicaid Act into law. For 60 years, these programs have delivered on a vital promise: access to health care for children, seniors, working families, and people in need. Today in #TX28, more than 179,000 people rely on Medicaid for their care.

But that promise is under attack. The new partisan budget law includes harmful cuts that threaten access to Medicare and Medicaid for millions of Americans.

I’m working in Congress to protect these programs and ensure families can continue to get the care they need.

This morning, I joined @GCHCTexas and @cityoflaredo Mayor Victor Treviño to celebrate National Health Center Week and award Gateway with a Congressional Recognition for their essential role in keeping South Texas healthy, strong, and connected.

As the third-largest healthcare provider in Laredo, Gateway delivers comprehensive care to tens of thousands of patients each year through a growing network of clinics across Webb, Zapata, and Jim Hogg Counties, offering vital services such as primary care, pediatrics, behavioral health, dental, and pharmacy support.

In Congress, I’ve secured over $14 million in federal funding to strengthen health services in South Texas, including $7.4 million to build the Webb County Southern Health Facility, $2 million for the West Laredo Clinic, $1.9 million for the Mines Road Clinic, and $3 million to support Gateway's operations.

Community Health Centers like Gateway do more than treat illness – they build trust, bridge gaps, and bring care directly to the people who need it most. I’ll keep working to ensure they have the support they need to continue serving #TX28 with dignity and compassion.

Republicans promised their budget wouldn’t touch seniors’ health care, but the nonpartisan @USCBO reports it could cut nearly $500 billion from Medicare by 2034.

On top of that, the budget slashes Medicaid and SNAP funding while adding $3.4 trillion to the deficit to fund tax breaks for the wealthiest 10%. The burden would fall hardest on seniors, low-income families, and rural communities – including many across #TX28 who rely on Medicare and Medicaid.

That’s why I strongly opposed this bill and will keep fighting to protect affordable, accessible health care for South Texans.

In the aftermath of Republicans' budget, South Texans are continuing to face threats to health care services, and the worst is still ahead.

In TX-28 alone, nearly 115,000 people are expected to pay more for insurance because of the elimination of premium tax credits. At the same time, deep reductions to Medicaid set for 2026 are already pressuring small hospitals to scale back operations or completely close their doors. Within a decade, rural areas could see $155 billion in Medicaid spending disappear, leaving communities vulnerable when they need help most.

These higher costs and reduced services will fall hardest on rural and working-class families, which is why I opposed this partisan budget. In Congress, I'll keep fighting to defend affordable health care, protect access to essential services, and ensure no one is left behind.
Read more from @USATODAY. ⬇️ https://t.co/opxqccnZ3Y

Seniors deserve access to early and comprehensive cancer screenings. That’s why I cosponsored the bipartisan Nancy Gardner Sewell Act to expand Medicare coverage for multi-cancer early detection tests.

This bill creates a clear path for @US_FDA-approved tests that can detect multiple cancers early – saving lives, improving outcomes, and lowering costs.

Cancer touches every family. I’ll keep working across the aisle to make sure seniors in South Texas and across the country have access to lifesaving innovations in cancer detection.

With vital health insurance tax credits under threat, monthly premiums for 113,000 people in #TX28 are set to skyrocket. The program serves everyone from small business owners to rural communities, and allowing it to expire could result in complete loss of coverage.

This tax credit makes affordable, quality health care possible for every South Texan. I’ll keep working with my colleagues in Congress to protect it and ensure families across our district can get the care they need without jeopardizing their financial security.

A government shutdown creates serious challenges for communities across the country. At stake are $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts, $500 billion in Medicare cuts, and threats to the Affordable Care Act that millions of Americans rely on. In my district, 113,000 people are directly affected. Families lose access to school lunches, Meals on Wheels, and SNAP benefits while monthly premiums rise.

This is not fiscal responsibility. It is misplaced priorities. I am in Washington, D.C., working to find a bipartisan solution, because at the end of the day it is everyday Americans who pay the price.

Read more from Border Report ⬇️

The government shutdown is going to affect communities nationwide. Healthcare and some Medicaid services experience interruptions. Many families risk losing access to essential health care, nutrition programs, and support services that they rely on every day.

These cuts put people last, not first. A bipartisan solution is the only way to protect families and communities and ensure Americans can access the services they need.

See more from @KGNSnews.⬇️

In Laredo, I hosted a roundtable on the impacts of the government shutdown across South Texas. We covered how the shutdown is affecting local families, federal employees, veterans, farmers, and small businesses, including the potential doubling of health insurance premiums for 113,000 residents in #TX28 if Affordable Care Act tax credits are not extended.

I addressed and corrected false claims about undocumented immigrants receiving federal health benefits, emphasizing the importance of honest and fact-based dialogue. I also shared that I signed a letter refusing my congressional pay. If nearly 15,000 federal employees in TX-28 are going without a paycheck, then neither will I.

The roundtable brought together several community partners and organizations supporting South Texans during this challenging time. I want to thank Mayor Treviño and everyone who joined the discussion for their insights and commitment to our community. 

A government shutdown doesn’t just affect politicians in Washington – it affects real people in our communities. It impacts families, delays paychecks for federal workers, and disrupts services people rely on. I will continue working with colleagues from both parties to find solutions and ensure stability for the people of South Texas.

A constituent recently shared that their monthly health insurance payment will rise from $767.65 in 2025 to $1,069.21 in 2026 – a 39% increase before any subsidies are applied. That’s an unsustainable jump for families trying to make ends meet.

This isn’t an isolated case. More than 113,000 of our neighbors in #TX28 will see premium increases next year, with even higher rate hikes expected. These rising costs are pricing people out of coverage and putting quality care further out of reach.

We can only fix this if Republicans and Democrats come to the negotiating table and work together on real solutions that keep costs low, expand access, and ensure Americans can rely on affordable, quality health care.

Texans battling a life-threatening illness should not have to wait for the care and security they’ve earned.

Too many patients face long delays before they can access Social Security Disability and Medicare benefits.

That’s why I’ve cosponsored the bipartisan Metastatic Breast Cancer Access to Care Act – to eliminate these harmful waiting periods and ensure patients receive vital income and coverage immediately.

This important bill is about compassion, fairness, and being there for patients when it matters most.

I voted to reopen the government because families in South Texas deserve reliable access to essential services and our federal workers deserve their paychecks.

The deal keeps WIC funded, suspends cuts to Medicaid hospital payments, and ensures community clinics like Gateway Community Health Center in Laredo can continue serving our community. It also gives Congress time to negotiate improvements to Affordable Care Act subsidies so families can keep the coverage they depend on.

On border security, my position is clear. Walls are a 14th century solution to a 21st century problem. Border crossings have fallen without new wall construction, and Laredo continues to report some of the lowest numbers in the country. Real security means listening to our agents and supporting new technology, river roads, and water barriers that work.
